article_sentences: Three months of lull established by security forces in Jammu and Kashmir was rattled by the back-to-back incidents of violence in the past six days.
On November 11, a terror attack on a checkpoint manned by the personnel of the Central Reserve.
Police Force (CRPF) in Kulgam left three jawans injured.
On November 16, a local, whom the police suspected of having joined the terror ranks a few days ago, was killed after six days of a siege-like anti-terror operation in residential areas of Kulgam.
In Jammu’s Kishtwar, two Special.
Police Officers (SPOs) of the J&K. Police were found dead with bullet wounds, a day after they were reported missing in a forest range on November 11.
The police and the Army, however, remain tight-lipped about the circumstances around the killing of these SPOs, and there are conflicting reports on the circumstances that led to their deaths.
The anti-terror operation in civilian areas of Kulgam has raised concerns.

Former J&K Chief Minister and PDP president Mehbooba Mufti described the operation, spread over six days, as “collective punishment that only breeds alienation and resentment,” while NC spokesman Imran Nabi Dar suggested that entire villages were put under prolonged restrictions for days.
The Omar Abdullah government, because of limited powers and no jurisdiction over the police in J&K, a Union Territory since 2019, finds itself hamstrung.
The iron hand policy to stamp out terrorism and separatism has been effective from a strictly security perspective — terror attacks as well as local recruitments into terror ranks have declined.
According to the police, local recruits have come down to single digit or fewer than 10 in Kashmir.

stories.headline: Akvan intensifies into severe cyclone near Andhra coast
stories.title: Akvan intensifies into severe cyclone near Andhra coast
stories.summary: Visakhapatnam, Nov 18 : Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’, looming over the central parts of South and adjoining Westcentral Bay of Bengal, has intensified into a severe cyclone, and is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts on Friday. According to India Meteorological Department (IMD) bulletin on Wednesday morning, the cyclonic storm moved very slowly north-northwestwards with the speed of three kmph during past six hours, intensified into a severe cyclonic storm and lay centered at 0530 hours at about 580 km east of Chennai (Tamil Nadu), 650 km northeast of Trincomalee (Sri Lanka), 610 km southeast of Machilipatnam (Andhra Pradesh), 610 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam (Andhra Pradesh) and 730 km south of Gopalpur (Odisha). Continuing to move north-northwestward, it is likely to cross Andhra Pradesh & Yanam coasts between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, around noon of November 20, as a severe cyclonic storm with the maximum sustained wind speed of 100-110 kmph gusting to 120 kmph. Prakhar Jain, Managing Director, Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority and Chief Executive Officer of Real Time Governance Society (RTGS), said that the cyclone movement is being continuously monitored. Appropriate instructions are being issued to the district administrations. He said 13 teams of NDRF, 11 teams of SDRF and local fire brigades were ready for emergency relief operations. Due to the impact of Tapan, there will be very heavy rains in some places in coastal districts on Thursday and Friday. Heavy to very heavy rains are likely at isolated places. APSDMA has appealed to people in the coastal region not to leave their homes unless it is an emergency. Farmers have been advised to take precautionary measures in agricultural work. Meanwhile, Home Minister V. Anita reviewed the situation as 'Akvan' intensified into a severe cyclonic storm. Officials reported that 'Akvan' is moving at a sluggish pace of 3 km/h. It is expected to make landfall by the afternoon of Friday. Home Minister Anita directed the state machinery to remain on high alert for the next 48 hours. She directed officials to take measures to prevent loss of life and property. The cyclone is likely to impact the North Andhra region. The public has been advised to remain vigilant. The Home Minister said residents in coastal areas should avoid stepping out unless absolutely necessary. Residents in low-lying areas must move to relief centres as soon as instructed by the authorities, she said. (IANS)

stories.title: ‘Akvan’ intensifies into severe cyclone, heading towards Andhra coast
stories.summary: ‘Akvan’ intensifies into severe cyclone, heading towards Andhra coast
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclonic Storm ‘Akvan’, which has intensified into a severe cyclonic storm over the Bay of Bengal, is expected to cross the Andhra Pradesh and Yanam coasts around noon on Friday, 20 November, prompting authorities to place coastal districts on high alert.
According to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), the cyclone was moving north-northwestwards at a slow speed of around 3 kmph during the six hours preceding its Wednesday morning bulletin.

At 5.30 am on Wednesday, the storm was centred over the west-central and adjoining southwest Bay of Bengal, approximately 580 km east of Chennai, 610 km southeast of Machilipatnam and 610 km south-southeast of Visakhapatnam.
The IMD said the system was likely to continue moving north-northwestwards before crossing the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Visakhapatnam, including Yanam, around noon on Friday.
At the time of landfall, the severe cyclonic storm is expected to bring maximum sustained winds of 100-110 kmph, with gusts reaching up to 120 kmph.
With the cyclone expected to affect coastal Andhra Pradesh, the state government has stepped up preparedness and emergency response arrangements.

Prakhar Jain, managing director of the Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) and Chief Executive Officer of the Real Time Governance Society (RTGS), said the movement of the cyclone was being continuously monitored.
He said instructions were being issued to district administrations to ensure preparedness and minimise potential damage.

As part of the emergency arrangements, 13 National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) teams and 11 State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) teams have been kept ready, along with local fire and emergency services.
The cyclone is expected to bring heavy rainfall across several coastal districts on Thursday and Friday.
According to the state disaster management authorities, very heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places, with some coastal areas potentially witnessing intense downpours.
The APSDMA has advised residents in coastal regions to remain indoors and avoid unnecessary travel.

Ms. Anitha, who reviewed the preparedness with officials on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), directed the State machinery to remain on high alert for the next 48 hours.
She asked officials to take all possible measures to prevent loss of life and property.

Since the cyclone is likely to cause considerable damage to infrastructure, the Minister asked the officials to stock sufficient equipment and materials as a precautionary measure.

He asked them to keep the public informed if power supply was shut off or if any disruptions occurred as part of precautionary measures.

stories.headline: Cyclone threat returns to Odisha, restrictions on beaches ahead of landfall
stories.title: Cyclone threat returns to Odisha, restrictions on beaches ahead of landfall
stories.summary: Cyclone threat returns to Odisha, restrictions on beaches ahead of landfall
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The IMD said cyclone Akvan is likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Visakhapatnam tomorrow.
It is expected to bring winds of 40-50 kmph to Odisha and the sea is likely to remain rough.

The Odisha government has restricted coastal tourism and beach recreation as the Bay of Bengal turned rough ahead of cyclone Akvan's expected landfall in neighbouring Andhra Pradesh on Friday, news agency Press Trust of India reported.

The India Meteorological Department said the severe cyclonic storm, with sustained winds of 100-110 kmph and gusts of up to 120 kmph, was likely to cross the Andhra Pradesh coast between Nellore and Visakhapatnam around noon tomorrow.
The cyclone is expected to bring winds of 40-50 kmph to Odisha on Thursday, rising to 50-60 kmph on Friday and Saturday.
The sea is likely to remain rough from Wednesday night to Saturday, the weather department said.
Following the warning, Odisha Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh P Patil asked the commissioner-cum-secretary of the tourism department to immediately enforce safety measures, according to PTI.

“There is an urgent need to safeguard tourists, visitors, tourism personnel and the general public from risks arising from rough seas, strong winds, heavy rainfall and coastal inundation,” Patil said in the letter.
He asked the tourism department to direct tourism authorities, operators, hotels, resorts and other stakeholders to suspend beach tourism and recreational activities at vulnerable coastal locations.
Boating, water sports, pleasure cruises and other sea-based tourist activities must also remain suspended until conditions are declared safe.
The departments concerned have been asked to restrict public access to unsafe beaches, seafronts, jetties and coastal viewing points.

“Direct hotels, resorts, tour operators and other tourism establishments in coastal areas to alert guests, avoid outdoor excursions, comply with evacuation or shelter directions and maintain emergency contacts and essential supplies,” the letter said.

stories.headline: As UP gears up for Assembly polls, ECI team to review election preparedness
stories.title: As UP gears up for Assembly polls, ECI team to review election preparedness
stories.summary: As UP gears up for Assembly polls, ECI team to review election preparedness
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The review, to be held in Agra, is part of the Election Commission's preparations for Assembly elections in Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab, Manipur and Goa.

A team of senior Election Commission officials will review Uttar Pradesh’s preparedness for the Assembly elections on November 19 as part of a phased assessment ahead of polls expected early next year, news agency Press Trust of India reported.

Officials told PTI that the team, led by a Senior Deputy Election Commissioner, had recently visited Meerut to assess the preparedness of election officials in some divisions of western Uttar Pradesh.
The review in the state is being conducted in phases.
The Election Commission has completed its review visits to Uttarakhand, Manipur and Punjab, while a visit to Goa is being planned.
While recently ordering a Special Summary Revision of electoral rolls in 17 states, the poll body noted that Assembly elections in the five states could take place "early next year."
The term of the 403-member Uttar Pradesh Assembly ends on May 22, 2027.
The terms of the Assemblies in Manipur, Goa, Punjab and Uttarakhand end on different dates in March 2027.
The Representation of the People Act, 1950, allows the Election Commission to hold elections earlier than six months before the end of an Assembly’s term.
As part of election preparations, Uttar Pradesh and Goa have also begun first-level checks of electronic voting machines and voter-verifiable paper audit trail units.

During these checks, engineers from Bharat Electronics Limited and Electronics Corporation of India Limited, the two public sector companies that manufacture the equipment, examine the machines for mechanical defects.
Faulty units are sent back to the manufacturers for repair or replacement.

stories.title: Supreme Court declines status quo against High Court allowing interim bail to Azam Khan

reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence

article_sentences: The Supreme Court declined an oral plea by the Directorate of Enforcement (ED) to immediately freeze an Allahabad High Court order granting interim bail to former Uttar Pradesh Minister and Samajwadi Party leader Mohammad Azam Khan in a money laundering case.
However, a Bench headed by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant agreed to urgently list the ED appeal on November 19.
The oral exchange happened during a mentioning made by Additional Solicitor General S.V. Raju, representing the ED, for early listing of the appeal.
Mr. Raju asked for a status quo in the meanwhile, but the apex court refused, with Justice Joymalya Bagchi remarking that “heavens will not fall, let him [Khan] be on interim bail”.

In its order granting interim bail on November 17, a Division Bench of the High Court found the arrest of Mr. Khan on October 31, at the very gates of jail as soon as he came out on bail in a PAN card case, both “motivated and malafide”.
This Bench concluded that the ED had not followed the necessary procedure of arrest.

article_sentences: The Supreme Court has transferred a large batch of land acquisition matters to the Delhi High Court for fresh adjudication.
The bench transferred the cases observing that it would not take up each case individually, because that would require a factual appreciation which would consume a lot of time.
A bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, and Justice V Mohana transferred the matters invoking Article 142 of the Constitution.
It revived the writ petitions and sent them to the High Court, requesting the Chief Justice of the Delhi High Court to assign a Division Bench that would hear the matters on a daily basis.

The matter relates to civil appeals, contempt petitions, miscellaneous applications, review petitions and curative petitions, concerning land in Delhi acquired by the Union government, the Delhi government, the Delhi Development Authority (DDA), the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC), the Airport Authority of India (AAI), and other agencies.
The bench noted that some acquisitions had been initiated as far back as in 1950.

All the acquisitions took place before 01.01.2014, when the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013 came into force, and were made under the Land Acquisition Act, 1894.

Provided that where an award has been made and compensation in respect of a majority of land holdings has not been deposited in the account of the beneficiaries, then, all beneficiaries specified in the notification for acquisition under section 4 of the said Land Acquisition Act, shall be entitled to compensation in accordance with the provisions of this Act.
In Pune Municipal Corporation v Harakchand Misirimal Solanki, it was held that an acquisition would lapse if either possession was not taken or compensation was not paid.
Landowners relied on this to obtain declarations of lapse from the High Court.
In Indore Development Authority v Manoharlal, a Constitution Bench held that both conditions must be met for lapse, namely that compensation was not deposited and possession was not taken.

This overruled Pune Municipal, which the bench observed as controversy that arose with regard to the orders passed by the High Court in the interregnum, meaning the period when the High Court relied on Pune Municipal.

stories.title: Maharashtra Cabinet approves cash rewards for information on weapons looted by Maoists
stories.summary: The decision comes amid the State government’s efforts to eliminate Left-wing extremism and accelerate development in areas previously affected by Maoist activities
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'cabinet approves' in title weight 44
candidate gate: no category but HIGH+ priority -> allowed
article_sentences: The Maharashtra Cabinet on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) approved a cash reward scheme for individuals providing information leading to the recovery of weapons looted by Maoists from security forces, with rewards of up to ₹1.5 lakh for individual weapons and sanctioning powers extending to ₹1 crore.
The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis.

According to the Chief Minister’s Office (CMO), the reward amount will depend on the type and number of weapons recovered, including automatic and semi-automatic firearms, other weapons and ammunition.
The government said Maoists had, over the years, looted weapons belonging to State security forces during attacks on police stations and police personnel.

While existing provisions provide rewards for information leading to the arrest of Maoists and additional financial assistance to those surrendering with weapons, there was no specific provision for rewarding individuals who helped recover weapons previously looted from security forces.
The Home Department subsequently proposed a separate reward mechanism to facilitate the recovery of these weapons, which received Cabinet approval on Tuesday (November 17, 2026).

Under the scheme, Superintendents of Police will have the authority to sanction rewards of up to ₹10 lakh, while the Deputy Inspector General of Police, Gadchiroli Range, can approve amounts exceeding ₹10 lakh and up to ₹25 lakh.

Rewards exceeding ₹25 lakh and up to ₹50 lakh will require approval from the Special Inspector General of Police, Anti-Naxal Operations, while the Additional Director General of Police (Special Operations) will be authorised to approve rewards exceeding ₹50 lakh and up to ₹1 crore.
The decision comes amid the State government’s efforts to eliminate Left-wing extremism and accelerate development in areas previously affected by Maoist activities.

In its statement, the government said coordinated efforts by the Centre and the State had weakened the influence of Maoist organisations in the region, particularly in Gadchiroli and Gondia, which it described as having become Naxal-free.
The government also said several development projects were being implemented in these districts as part of efforts to transform areas previously affected by Left-wing extremism.

stories.title: Supreme Court To Hear Plea Seeking Removal Of Videos Of Italian Politician Questioning Indian Elections At Bharat Summit
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court on Wednesday agreed to list a plea seeking the removal of social media videos featuring an Italian politician allegedly questioning the country's democratic system during the Bharat Summit 2026 organised by the Telangana Government in Hyderabad on November 13-14.

The matter was mentioned before Chief Justice of India Surya Kant by Advocate Syed Rizwan Ahmad, who sought urgent intervention to take down the videos featuring Giacomo Filibeck, Secretary-General of the Party of European Socialists.

Describing the remarks as a direct intervention in India's democratic affairs, the counsel said that the Italian delegate had not only raised the slogan but also translated it for other delegates attending the event.
"There was a summit organised by the main Opposition.
Foreign invitees were also there and one person from Italy, he represents the European Socialist Party, directly intervened in the bona fide Indian democratic system.
He used a very abusive slogan, since the urgency is of pulling down that slogan from social media, I need not repeat it here.

And it appears, the Italian delegate translates the slogan for other delegates, and on my soil he is saying the government is corrupt here and it is not bona fide and that he will work with the opposition to restore democracy.
It is a grave violation; it requires your intervention to pull down the video," Ahmed submited.
Responding to the mentioning, CJI Surya Kant asked whether the matter could be listed on the day after Friday.
The counsel agreed.
"Rest you argue before the concerned bench," the CJI said.

article_sentences: The Delhi Cabinet on Tuesday (November 17, 2026) approved one-time financial assistance of ₹1 lakh each to around 500 Pollution Under Control Certificate (PUCC) issuing centres for improving their infrastructure, as per the Chief Minister’s Office.
The assistance will support the upgradation and modernisation of these centres and the government is expected to spend approximately ₹5 crore on the initiative.
Chief Minister Rekha Gupta said that controlling air pollution in Delhi remains one of the government’s key priorities.
“Modern infrastructure, transparent testing procedures and effective monitoring are essential to ensuring cleaner air.

Equipping vehicle pollution testing centres with modern facilities and bringing uniformity to their operations will strengthen the government’s efforts to control pollution,” Ms. Gupta said, adding that the aim is to make the PUC testing system more organised, transparent and reliable.

The CM said that stronger CCTV surveillance will make it easier to monitor the testing process, enhancing transparency and accountability at the centres and will also strengthen public confidence in the PUC certification system.

A CAG report tabled in the Delhi Assembly in April last year had said there were significant “discrepancies” in the Pollution Under Control (PUC) certification system, and many vehicle owners were not getting their vehicles checked as per norms.
These centres check vehicle emissions and issue Pollution Under Control Certificates (PUCCs).

The unorganised development of the PUCC centres has resulted in a lack of uniformity in infrastructure, testing facilities, signboards, external appearance and monitoring arrangements, making effective supervision difficult, the CMO said in a statement.
“Inadequate CCTV coverage has also led to allegations of improper issuance of PUCCs and other irregularities.
The scheme aims to address these shortcomings by bringing all authorised PUC centres in line with uniform prescribed standards and making the testing system more transparent and organised.
Where a PUC centre tests all three categories of vehicles, it is technically treated as a single centre,” the statement said.

stories.headline: J-K CM inaugurates, lays foundation for 13 projects worth Rs 92.84 crore in Poonch
stories.title: J-K CM inaugurates, lays foundation for 13 projects worth Rs 92.84 crore in Poonch
stories.summary: Mendhar, Nov 18: Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah on Wednesday laid the foundation stones and inaugurated 13 development projects worth Rs 92.84 crore in the border town of Mendhar in Poonch district, aimed at strengthening infrastructure and improving public service delivery. The projects cover key sectors, including power, flood protection, road connectivity, education and water supply, an official spokesman said. He said the projects include the laying of foundation stones for a 50 MVA Grid Sub-Station at Mendhar and flood protection works along Mendhari Nallah, besides key infrastructure projects in road connectivity, education and water supply. During the programme, the chief minister also flagged off Jammu and Kashmir State Road Transport Corporation (SRTC) bus services on three new routes and two new water tankers to improve public transport and drinking water supply in Mendhar. The spokesman said the chief minister's visit underscored the government's commitment to strengthening essential infrastructure, improving public services and accelerating development in remote and border areas of Jammu and Kashmir.
